title: Effectively closed classes and diagonal avoidance

based_on.title: Computability theory
based_on.pages: Version 2024-02-25; §23.1 opening DNC definition, p.86; §23.2 Lemma 23.4 and Theorem 23.5, pp.86–87; common-stage repair of the tree conversion

summary: Represent enumerable forbidden prefixes by computable binary trees, then find noncomputable binary functions that avoid every defined self-computation.
abstract: An infinite sequence of zeros and ones may have to avoid an enumerable list of forbidden finite patterns at its beginning. Each prohibition is finite, even though checking every restriction describes a collection of infinite sequences. Such a collection is called effectively closed. It can always be represented by a computable binary tree: longer candidate words must recheck their short prefixes for newly discovered prohibitions. This gives a way to choose a permitted sequence using the halting oracle whenever any permitted sequence exists. Diagonal avoidance provides a concrete example: at each program number, choose a bit different from that program's output on itself, if it stops. These choices are exactly the separators of the familiar diagonal output sets. They form a nonempty effectively closed class, yet no computable sequence can make all the required choices.
